mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority of the UBO's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or financial institution in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, together with notarial certification of signature and copy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and current register of shareholders and directors for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry or corporate secretary in the corporate shareholder's country of establishment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; translation into French, German, or English by a sworn translator for Luxembourg filing

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial owner declaration form under Article 9 of the amended Law of 13 January 2019
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / notary admitting the declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signature before a Luxembourg notary; no apostille required for Luxembourg-origin notarial deeds

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds declaration for each shareholder and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: External financial institution holding the relevant relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if issued outside the EU/EEA

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or police clearance certificate for UBOs (if we require enhanced due diligence)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Criminal records registry or commercial registry in the UBO's country of nationality or residence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory initial and continuous risk-based screening of UBOs, directors, and senior managers against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, and Luxembourg national sanctions and restrictive measures lists. PEP screening is mandatory for foreign politically exposed persons under Chapter 5 of the AML/CFT Law and CSSF Regulation 12-02; enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth verification, and senior management approval must apply to senior PEPs, high-risk third-country relationships, and unusual transaction patterns.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – www.lbr.lu; RCS filings may be initiated via MyGuichet.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A SARL company name must be expressed in Latin alphabet characters; a non-Latin or non-Roman-script name must be accompanied by an official transliteration. The name must not create confusion with existing registered names, must not be contrary to public order or good morals, and must include the obligatory legal suffix 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or 'SARL' (or 'S.à r.l.'). French, German, and English are the customary accepted languages.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon official rejection of the proposed company name, the applicant or notary shall: (1) obtain from the LBR/RCS a written statement of refusal specifying the conflicting identical or confusingly similar name; (2) within 30 days of the refusal, file through a notary or directly via MyGuichet.lu an amended name reservation together with a covering justification the existing registration does not cause confusion, or propose a corrected name; (3) if the amended name remains refused, lodge an administrative appeal with the Administrative Tribunal of Luxembourg (Tribunal administratif) within 3 months of notification of the final rejection, in accordance with the amended code of administrative procedure; legal representation by a Luxembourg-bar attorney is mandatory for the administrative appeal; alternatively, submit a completely new name-clearing application and begin a fresh 90-day reservation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as a statutory seat for a regulated P2P micro-lending platform. Luxembourg law requires the registered office to be a genuine physical office situated in Luxembourg, capable of receiving official correspondence and maintaining board minutes, accounts, and statutory records. A virtual office may be used only as an ancillary contact address, but cannot replace physical management presence or satisfy CSSF substance expectations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: estimated 80% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 12 months after license application or authorization, given the high-risk ISIC 6499 micro-lending sector and the intensive AML/CFT supervision exercised by the CSSF.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, notably Articles 1, 6, 13, 20 and 100-1 et seq. (SARL provisions); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register and the Official Broadcasting of Legal Information.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg City
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation and articles of association (acte constitutif / statuts) filed with and registered by the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum registered capital is EUR 12,000 for a SARL; the full amount must be subscribed, and cash contributions blocked until legal effectiveness. A bank certificate confirming the blocked account, opened in the company's name 'en formation', is required; contributions in kind require a statutory auditor's certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the articles of association and incorporation deed of the Société à Responsabilité Limitée, including the subscription of the full share capital of EUR 12,000 held in the designated blocked bank account, are hereby approved and adopted. RESOLVED, that the registered office is established at [Registered Office Address], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, to which the Luxembourg courts shall have exclusive jurisdiction. RESOLVED, that [Name of Manager] is appointed as sole manager (gérant), with full authority to represent the company, open accounts, and effect any incorporation filings before the Luxembourg Business Registers and all competent administrations, and any such filing and execution already completed on behalf of the company is ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Pre-Incorporation Due Diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) via the RCS portal (e-Request)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online name-reservation request containing up to three proposed company names, the planned legal form (SARL), and the intended activities. The reserved name must contain 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or 'SARL' suffix and be sufficiently distinctive. The LBR will issue a name-reservation certificate valid for a defined period.
required_dossiers: Completed name-reservation request form
Copy of passports/national identity cards of all shareholders
Details of proposed registered activity (ISIC/NACE code)
Power of attorney if filed through an authorized intermediary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to identity or similarity with a prior right, the applicant may file amended alternative names with additional evidence of distinctiveness, or appeal to the Luxembourg administrative courts within one month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Bank Account and Share Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution selected by the founders (RBC, BIL, BGL BNP Paribas or commercial banks)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account (compte bloqué) in the name of 'SARL en formation' and deposit the entire subscribed capital (minimum EUR 12,000) in cash. Provide the draft notarial incorporation deed and details of ultimate beneficial owners for AML/KYC clearance. The bank issues a certificate of capital blocking, which is made available to the notary before signing.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association
AML/KYC documentation for each shareholder
Source of funds and source of wealth declarations
Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) confirmation
Business plan summary for platform lending activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional documentation or questions the source of wealth, supply supplementary banking references or audited statements; if adverse credit decision remains, select another licensed Luxembourg credit institution and re-open the blocking account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Notarial Incorporation Deed and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary chosen by the founders (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary verifies the incorporation plan, the blocked capital certificate, the eligibility of directors/managers and the legality of the SARL's clauses. The notarial deed must be signed by all founders or their representatives, after which the notary executes and delivers the official certified copy (expédition). The articles take effect upon registration; pre-registration transactions can be ratified.
required_dossiers: Draft incorporation deed and articles of association
Bank certificate establishing the blocked capital
Passports/IDs of all shareholders and intended managers
UBO declarations
Certificate of name reservation
Criminal record extracts of managers if requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary homologates conditions or requests amendments, execute a supplemental deed or correct clauses before signing; a rejected deed can be rectified and resubmitted within five business days to the same notarial office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registry Filing, Publication and UBO Disclosure
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarial deed and registered office details with the RCS via the electronic filing platform. Request publication of the legal notice in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA) and complete the UBO register filing in accordance with Law of 13 January 2019. The RCS assigns the company registration number and issues an excerpt of the registration.
required_dossiers: Notarial incorporation deed (expédition)
UBO registration declaration
Proof of registered office address (lease or ownership title)
Application for RCS registration signed by manager(s)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS queries scarce or inconsistent filings, provide a supplementary conformed copy or an explanatory letter signed by manager within eight days; if the electronic publication is rejected, re-submit after correcting metadata using the existing deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT, Direct Tax and Social Security Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration with the RCS, file the application for a Luxembourg VAT number with the AEDT, submit the company file to the direct tax office (bureau d'imposition) for corporate income tax and municipal business tax, and register as an employer with the CCSS. The platform will be assigned with a VAT and tax identification number.
required_dossiers: RCS excerpt (extrait of registration)
Articles of association
Identity documents of shareholders and managers
Company bank account details
Power of attorney for tax agents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registrations are delayed or rejected because of inconsistent company status, provide an updated RCS excerpt and re-file with the correct domicile; administrative objections may be filed with the director of the competent administration within three months.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), Financial and Technical Licensing Division; Ministry of Economy for non-financial site permits if applicable
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Crowdfunding and P2P Lending Platform License under Regulation (EU) 2020/1503 (ECSP) and the Law of 12 May 2016 on crowdfunding, together with a special e-money or payment institution permit if the platform holds funds or executes payments.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement - Environment Agency Luxembourg
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 4 - EIA not required (office-only non-industrial activity); environmental registration and waste declarations apply
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC process emissions; office wastewater must meet municipal sewer discharge standards; electronic and battery waste is collected by approved recyclers pursuant to the Law of 21 March 2017 on waste; servers/IT assets must be disposed of under WEEE compliance and the Circular Economy Law.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for the registered office by the Grand Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps (CGI); compliance with building load-bearing capacity and occupational health requirements verified by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM); company must obtain the autorisation d'exploitation from the commune if the building is used for commercial/office purposes.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) (Luxembourg Inland Revenue) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; national electronic portals: myGuichet.lu, impotsdirects.public.lu, pvat.public.lu, and the AEDT e-filing/e-TVA platform; VIES database maintained by the Luxembourg VAT administration for intra-Community verifications.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Luxembourg-resident SARL is registered with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) on incorporation and receives a national identification number (matricule), which serves as the corporate tax identification number (NIF/TIN). For VAT, the SARL must file the official VAT registration application (Formulaire 645 / Demande d'immatriculation à la TVA) with the AEDT before commencing taxable supplies; the AEDT issues a Luxembourg VAT identification number with the 'LU' prefix (LU + 8 digits + 2 check digits). A non-resident foreign entity supplying taxable fintech or lending services in Luxembourg and not covered by the reverse charge must appoint a Luxembourg tax representative (representant responsable solidaire) and submit the same registration form through myGuichet.lu, attaching certified copies of the certificate of incorporation, articles of association (statuts), home-country trade register extract, identity documents of directors/managers, and a description of the intended activities. Registration must be perfected before the first taxable supply; late registration exposes the entity to penalties and interest but does not invalidate the underlying transactions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - A Luxembourg-resident SARL with registered office (siège statutaire) and central administration in Luxembourg is subject to unlimited corporate income tax liability (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités, IRC) on worldwide profits, plus the 7% solidarity surcharge (contribution au fonds de chômage) and municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal), yielding an aggregate effective rate of approximately 24.94% in Luxembourg City (17% IRC + 1.19% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax). No look-through or transparent taxation applies to a commercial P2P micro-lending SARL; taxable profits include interest margins, origination fees, underwriting commissions, platform fees and ancillary lending charges, reduced by arm's length operating, financing, AML-compliance, technology and bad-debt costs under article 109 LIR.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not provide a US-style check-the-box election. Relevant elections for a commercial SARL micro-lending platform: (i) application of the Luxembourg participation exemption (régime mère-fille) evidenced through the corporate tax return and holding documentation; (ii) option to waive the article 57 small-business VAT franchise and apply normal taxation; (iii) election to form a VAT group (assujettissement unique) on application to the AEDT for closely linked taxable persons (available since 1 January 2019); (iv) article 110 LIR election for roll-over deferral on reinvested capital gains; and (v) mandatory ATAD-compliant hybrid mismatch provisions (no elective mechanism), although symmetrical treatment of hybrid instruments may be achieved through contractual design of subordination, profit participation and conversion rights in the loan agreements, subject to general anti-abuse review.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) - Luxembourg VAT Code (Loi du 12 février 1979 concernant la taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, 'LVAT') implementing Council Directive 2006/112/EC; administered by the AEDT
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 30,000 (annual taxable turnover, exclusive of VAT) - small-business franchise under article 57 LVAT; registration is compulsory irrespective of turnover for taxable supplies subject to reverse charge, for intra-Community acquisitions exceeding EUR 10,000, for distance sales, or where the entity opts for full VAT taxation. A non-resident supplier without a Luxembourg fixed establishment must nevertheless register for Luxembourg VAT (or appoint a tax representative) when making taxable supplies in Luxembourg falling outside the general reverse-charge mechanism.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No general real-time fiscal clearance, API-based government clearance or digital stamping mandate exists in Luxembourg for B2B/B2C transactions. Electronic invoicing is permitted on mutual consent and is mandatory only for B2G supplies through the PEPPOL network (law on electronic invoicing in public markets, phased in since 1 January 2022). VAT returns (form TVA), EC sales lists (VIES) and Intrastat declarations must be e-filed through the AEDT/myGuichet portal using structured XML attachments. The P2P lending platform must preserve all electronic invoices and transaction-level records in original format for 10 years and make them accessible for AEDT/ACD audits.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% export VAT applies to (a) goods physically exported outside the EU by the supplier or a non-established purchaser within three months of supply (article 42 LVAT), supported by a validated customs export declaration and transport documents evidencing exit from the EU customs territory; (b) B2B services supplied to a customer established outside the EU, which are taxable at the customer's place of establishment (article 56 LVAT), including algorithm underwriting, loan-origination, platform-access, credit-scoring and data-processing services provided from Luxembourg to non-EU borrowers and platform users; and (c) in the P2P micro-lending context, interest income, loan-origination fees and credit intermediation services are VAT-exempt financial services (article 135(1)(b)-(d) of Directive 2006/112/EC) with no input VAT recovery, while platform fees effectively consumed outside the EU fall outside Luxembourg VAT scope. The platform must contemporaneously document the non-EU establishment of each counterparty through a valid foreign tax identification number, registered-office address, AML/KYC file and, where applicable, a tax residency certificate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/DAU) validated electronically through the Luxembourg Customs and Excise Agency (PLDA/ECS system) with proof of exit from the EU customs territory
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill or CMR international consignment note evidencing physical dispatch of goods outside the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank transfer confirmation, SWIFT MT103, or lender-funded disbursement record) evidencing receipt of export proceeds or non-EU customer payments
Commercial invoice and underlying loan agreement for P2P lending fees, underwriting commissions and platform charges
Packing list and weighing/quantity certificate for any goods-related transactions
Proof of customer's non-EU establishment: foreign trade register extract, VAT/tax identification certificate, or tax residency certificate (certificat de résidence fiscale)
Transport manifests, CIM rail consignment note, or EUR.1/certificate of origin where preferential customs origin is claimed
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg law does not impose an express statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline; the 180-day figure is applied as the commercial and arm's length benchmark for collection of export receivables and platform fees, consistent with Luxembourg transfer-pricing practice (article 56bis LIR). Where export zero-rating is claimed abusively (goods never exported, fictitious transport documents, services effectively consumed in Luxembourg), the AEDT issues a post-clearance assessment (redressement) recharging VAT at the standard 17% rate, with monthly late interest of 0.6% (7.2% per annum) and a non-payment majoration of up to 10% of the tax due. Deliberate tax fraud is criminally punishable under the Luxembourg law of 17 March 2016 with imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and/or a fine of up to EUR 250,000, plus confiscation of the tax advantage and possible publication of the judgment. The ordinary VAT assessment limitation period is 5 years, extended to 10 years in cases of established fraud, allowing retrospective clawback of older zero-rated transactions. Directors, statutory managers and the appointed tax representative may be held jointly and severally liable (article 53 AO) for unremitted VAT and penalty amounts of the SARL.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for financial-sector FX compliance; the BCL compiles external statistics and applies EU Capital Movements Directive (88/361/EEC) liberalisation, with no autonomous Luxembourg foreign-exchange control regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a fully liberalised jurisdiction within the EU Single Market; the euro is freely convertible for both current and capital account transactions. Profit remittances are unrestricted, subject only to standard AML/KYC validation and corporate formalities (board approval, audited accounts, and withholding tax compliance on dividends, where applicable). No exchange control approval is needed for inward or outward transfers, but all cross-border payments above EUR 12,500 require balance-of-payments reporting to the BCL via the domestic banking system; the P2P lending platform must file periodic BOP statements for non-EEA investors and borrowers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender requirement exists under Luxembourg law. Entities may freely retain, convert, or remit export receipts and service fees. The only obligation is bookkeeping and tax declaration accuracy under the Luxembourg Commercial Code and CIT law; for an ISIC 6499 financial services platform, loan repayments and interest income are classified as services/financial income and are not subject to any mandatory conversion or retention timeline.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and dedicated collection/payout sub-accounts

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account for high-net-worth investor flows
Cross-border clearing account, treasury concentration account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium. A Luxembourg-licensed Payment Institution (PI) or Electronic Money Institution (EMI) authorised by the CSSF under the Loi du 10 novembre 2009 is viable for domestic SEPA processing; however, offshore digital EMIs lacking a Luxembourg branch or passporting under PSD2 face legal barriers to clearing inbound loan repayments and outbound disbursements in EUR. Offshore EMIs may provide ancillary multi-currency virtual IBANs, but cannot serve as the primary regulated clearing rail for retail lending because the SARL must isolate client funds in a CSSF-approved segregation scheme and maintain supervisory compliance. Use of an unauthorised non-EEA EMI is prohibited.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg banks generally require at least one authorised signatory (typically a director with ultimate beneficial ownership) to attend a physical onboarding interview at the bank's registered office. Remote opening is possible only through Luxembourg's qualified electronic identification scheme (LuxTrust certificate) or an equivalent eIDAS-recognised eID, provided the director has an existing relationship or the bank offers an out-of-country video-verification process (rare and discretionary). A full in-person meeting is mandatory to open escrow/regulated accounts for high-risk ISIC 6499 micro-lending platforms; non-resident directors must appear before a notary or banking officer to attest identity, source of wealth, and the platform's anti-money-laundering controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Regulatory license verification block: bank refuses onboarding pending CSSF licence approval or because the SARL operates a P2P lending marketplace without a licence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide authenticated CSSF authorisation for the micro-lending activity, or, if operating under the crowdfunding intermediary exemption, a certified legal opinion confirming the activity falls within the 'crowdfunding services' scope of CSSF Circular 21/788 and EU Regulation 2020/1503; include the SARL's constitutive deed, statutes, and business plan classifying loans as balance-sheet lending or pure intermediation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds ambiguity for inbound investor capital, particularly non-EEA high-risk jurisdiction flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain a transactional audit trail: bank statements, investor onboarding KYC files, proof of underlying loan contracts, automated underwriting logs, and a custodian-segregated ledger evidencing each investor's source of wealth and source of funds; provide notarised affidavits for beneficial owners of >25% shareholders, plus FATF alignment and tax-residency certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Terrorist financing and sanctions screening red flag due to P2P lending across multiple currencies to retail borrowers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit live AML/CFT policy, automated sanctions-screening tool audit reports, transaction-monitoring rules, and evidence of screening against EU, UN, OFAC separately (for USD traffic), and CSSF lists; demonstrate dynamic borrower/investor risk scoring and an independent AML officer appointment under the 2004 AML Law.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Negative news or regulatory enforcement history associated with the lending platform or its directors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Obtain a comprehensive due-diligence report from a reputable screening provider; produce court-pending litigation register extracts from the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS), criminal record certificates from country of residence, and a valid professional indemnity insurance certificate (EUR 5 million+).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspicion of layering or commingling of operational funds with client escrow funds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a notarised escrow agreement, bank confirmation of separate operational and client-money accounts, monthly independent audit of the reconciliation process, and a legal opinion under CSSF Circular 21/788 requiring funds segregation; include evidence of daily automated reconciliation and sub-ledger integrity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For equity or shareholder loan injections: use SWIFT MT103 via the BCL TARGET2-SECURITIES infrastructure or SEPA wire if the sender is EEA-based; the EU Common Reporting Standard requires clear reference to the Payment Purpose Code – for Luxembourg BOP purposes, use purpose code 'ND0' for capital investment (direct investment) or 'F.6' for loans. For investor subscriptions into the P2P platform: each inbound transfer must be tagged with the loan/investment reference and include a statement of the beneficial owner; banks will require proof of the underlying investment agreement. Non-EEA inbound transfers in EUR or USD should be routed through a correspondent bank with SWIFT MT103 covering an intermediary bank; strict use of ISO 20022 remittance information is required, and any proceeds funding the platform must not exceed the authorised payment-to-payment timeline defined in the CSSF licence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Loan disbursements to retail borrowers must be executed via SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) for euro-area disbursements (max EUR 100,000 per transaction) or via SEPA Credit Transfer for sums above instant limits. For disbursements to non-EEA beneficiaries, use SWIFT MT103 with instruction 'OUR' (charges borne by sender) to ensure full settlement. Commercial letters of credit (UCP600) are applicable only for genuine trade flows, not consumer microloans; an ISIC 6499 P2P platform must use standard payment initiation services through its licensed bank or a regulated PI. Each disbursement must embed a structured creditor reference (e.g., loan number + repayment schedule) to permit automated reconciliation and satisfy the CSSF's obligation to trace funds. Settlement balances above EUR 100,000 must be held with the BCL or a commercial bank participant in T2 to ensure finality.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD spot and outright forward contracts (up to 12 months) with a Luxembourg-licensed bank, used to hedge non-EEA investor distributions
EUR/GBP cross-currency swap for UK borrower/pool funding, if the platform accepts GBP retail repayments
FX options (plain vanilla EUR/USD, EUR/CHF) for hedging contingent exposures from investor capital commitments

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not commonly available in Luxembourg due to full convertibility of EUR; however, for funding legacy assets in convertibility-restricted currencies (e.g., offshore renminbi), a NDF may be entered with a CSSF-authorized bookrunner, provided it does not create a speculative open position exceeding 12 months and is documented as a hedging-only instrument under ESMA EMIR rules

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (comptes annuels) – balance sheet, profit and loss account, and notes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM approval within 6 months after financial year-end; filing within 1 month of approval; for calendar-year SARL, practical deadline is 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal notice, court-ordered fines up to EUR 2,500, director personal liability, and administrative strike-off if annual accounts remain unfiled for two consecutive years.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités, IRC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year entity, filed by 30 June of the following year; for split-year accounts, the last day of the sixth month after year-end; extensions available on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 0.6% per month on unpaid tax; administrative late-filing penalties; criminal liability for fraudulent non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal business tax return (impôt commercial communal, ICC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same statutory window as the corporate income tax return (generally 30 June following the year); no separate municipal filing is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest of 0.6% per month; administrative penalties up to 200% of the assessed municipal tax in cases of wilful default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Net wealth tax return (impôt sur la fortune, IFT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual return with the corporate tax filing by 30 June following the tax year (or sixth month after year-end for non-calendar periods)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing forfeits statutory exemptions; default interest at 0.6% per month; additional assessments based on official documentation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT summary return (déclaration annuelle TVA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 30 April following the calendar year; monthly or quarterly filers must align their residual annual payment reconciliation by that date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty up to EUR 750 per return; default interest of 0.6% per month; criminal fines for deliberate misdeclaration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CSSF annual supervisory report and audited financial statements (for licensed financial-sector P2P lender)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the financial year-end (i.e., by 30 June for calendar-year entities), together with the statutory auditor's report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CSSF administrative pecuniary sanctions, suspension or revocation of the P2P lending license, and possible removal from the approval register.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit by an approved réviseur d'entreprises is compulsory if the SARL exceeds two of three thresholds: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, average employees 50. Furthermore, licensed financial-sector entities (including P2P micro-lending platforms) are subject to CSSF audit requirements regardless of these thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Lux GAAP), as transposed by the Law of 19 December 2002 (Commercial Code), constitutes the applicable accounting framework; consolidated or publicly listed groups may use IFRS; CSSF-supervised firms must comply with CSSF chart-of-accounts and reporting formats.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Luxembourg does not require an annual UBO re-filing. Under the Law of 13 January 2019, beneficial ownership information must be filed with the RBE within 30 days of any change. The SARL shall perform an annual internal review of its register of members, director changes, and UBO data; if changes are identified, an RBE update within 30 days. Where no change occurs, a documented no-change confirmation is held in the corporate records.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 2,000 – USD 6,000 per year for a Luxembourg registered office / corporate service agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 – USD 25,000 per year for a small/medium SARL subject to CSSF audit requirements

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined (17% corporate income tax, 7% solidarity/employment fund surcharge, and communal business tax for Luxembourg City)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No sector-specific holiday for P2P micro-lending. Applicable general incentives include the intellectual property (IP) box regime granting an 80% exemption on qualifying IP income, the participation exemption eliminating tax on dividends and capital gains from qualifying shareholdings, a 20% R&D tax credit, investment tax credits up to 12%, and the deduction of Luxembourg net wealth tax for corporate income tax purposes.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 170 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) submitted electronically via the e-Tax portal (MyGuichet.lu / Administration des Contributions Directes ACD).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within five months after the end of the financial year; for a calendar-year SARL the return is due by 31 May of the following year. A justified extension may be granted but in no case later than 31 December of the following fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: RCS registration number, legal form (SARL), registered office, VAT number, and corporate mailing address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Luxembourg-resident SARL with foreign shareholders, enter the local permanent establishment address and the appointed tax representative's details. No separate non-resident registration is required because the SARL is the taxable taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable result from the commercial year: net profit/loss per the audited financial statements before tax, adjusted for deductible and non-deductible charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the SARL is owned by non-residents, all Luxembourg-source P2P lending income (loan interest spread, origination fees, late payment penalties, and bad debt recoveries) must be declared; foreign-owned intra-group provisions are scrutinised for arm's length deductibility.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions: interest paid, service fees, software/technology royalties, salaries, depreciation, bad debt provisions, and net wealth tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident lenders or shareholders supplying funding or systems to the SARL must provide proper contracts, CbC-relevant documentation, and proof that the charge is not a hidden profit distribution. Interest and royalties paid by a Luxembourg SARL are generally exempt from Luxembourg withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments: related-party transfer pricing adjustments, ATAD interest limitation, participation exemption, and tax depreciation recapture.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach schedule showing arm's length remuneration for loan origination, algorithmic underwriting, credit scoring, and collection services performed by foreign affiliate companies. Lack of a contemporaneous benchmark may trigger an ACD adjustment and penalty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carry-forward offset, including the source year of each loss and the total amount of prior tax losses being used in the current period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders cannot claim the SARL's losses against their own tax returns. The loss carry-forward is deductible only against future Luxembourg taxable income of the same entity and is capped at the five-year carry-forward period.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a fixed administrative fine of up to EUR 3,000 at the ACD's discretion, monthly late-payment interest of 0.6% on the unpaid tax, and a 10% late-payment surcharge. If no return is filed within two months, the tax office may assess taxable income ex officio with an additional 50% penalty. Fraudulent non-declaration further exposes the company to criminal fines and imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must apply for relief at source by submitting the official request with the Luxembourg ACD before dividend distribution, attaching a tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the shareholder's jurisdiction and a declaration of beneficial ownership. Luxembourg may grant a reduced or zero withholding rate under the relevant double taxation agreement (DTA). If tax is withheld at the statutory 15%, the shareholder may file a refund claim with the ACD within five years of the end of the calendar year in which withholding occurred.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 0% withholding tax on outbound interest and 0% on royalties paid by a Luxembourg SARL to non-residents, provided the payment is made to a beneficial owner not resident in a blacklisted jurisdiction. Treaty rates generally also provide 0% for interest (EU Interest-Royalties Directive) and 0% to 10% for royalties, depending on the DTA.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File is required when the group's consolidated annual turnover exceeds EUR 750,000,000. Local File is required when the Luxembourg entity is a member of a multinational group with intra-group transactions exceeding EUR 1,000,000 annually, per Luxembourg ACD Circular LIR 170/2. For this P2P micro-lending platform, any intercompany fee for origination, credit scoring, or funding exceeding EUR 500,000 must be supported by a contemporaneous arm's length benchmark.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply offshore-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR). Instead, substance is assessed under OECD/ATAD principles, Article 56 LIR, and the GAAR. The micro-lending SARL must maintain real premises, qualified staff, board decision-making on loan policies, origination algorithms, risk underwriting, and servicing functions in Luxembourg. A letterbox company may be disregarded, with profits re-attributed to the actual control seat.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission from Form 170 of P2P loan origination fees, net interest spread, recovery income, or default penalties; fabrication of management fees or fake bad-debt allowances to shift profit offshore.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of the full evaded tax plus a penalty of 50% of that tax; criminal fine up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years under Articles 396-399 of the Luxembourg Criminal Code and the General Tax Law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve fraudulent returns are personally liable for the corporate tax shortfall on the basis of 'faute caractérisée' (Article 7 Civil Code, Article 180 Abgabenordnung). Courts may apply veil piercing, asset forfeiture, director disqualification, travel bans, and imprisonment for directors found to have organised the fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the micro-lending SARL with no real employees, no strategic decision-making in Luxembourg, offshored servers and underwriting algorithms, and using circular funding structures solely to claim Luxembourg treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax administration disregards the entity under GAAR and Article 56 LIR; taxable income is re-attributed to the shareholder jurisdiction; a hidden distribution is recharacterised and taxed at 15% withholding plus late interest; administrative fines up to EUR 25,000 for failure to disclose substance indicators.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly and severally liable for the resulting Luxembourg tax arrears if they knowingly used the entity as a shield. Luxembourg courts may lift limited liability due to abuse of law, impose travel bans, block bank accounts, and order directors to pay unpaid taxes and fines personally.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a P2P consumer lending platform without the required financial-sector license or consumer credit authorisation from the CSSF; processing loans through unregulated wallets; failing to conduct KYC/beneficial ownership checks; laundering proceeds of fraud through the platform.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative sanction up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover imposed by the CSSF; criminal money-laundering penalties under Article 506-1 of the Criminal Code include imprisonment of 5 to 10 years and fines up to EUR 5,000,000; the court may also order public publication of the sanction and dissolution of the entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the absence of AML controls. They face criminal imprisonment, personal fines, asset freezes, travel bans, disqualification from management functions, and extradition proceedings in cross-border cases. The corporate veil is pierced where the SARL was used as a conduit for illicit lending funds.
